result.title: Who Is the Influencer? Consensus Dynamics in Multi-Agent Systems
result.summary: Multi-agent LLM systems are increasingly used in practice, but their behavior is complex and hard to understand. We design a simple task to ask which model has the most influence on the final consensus when several models are mixed in one system. Experimentally, across seven model families, we find that the opinions of the other models are absorbed into the opinion of the stronger model, the one with more parameters. This happens even though the task requires no pretraining knowledge and has no correct answer. To understand this phenomenon, we interpret the agents as weighted particles moving on a simplex. Larger models carry a larger weight and therefore occupy a deeper well in the energy landscape. A large weight means strong in-context learning: a model with a large weight amplifies the majority of its context. Larger models are generally better at in-context learning, and this is what makes the larger model the influencer. We hope that this work helps to interpret multi-agent systems, whose behavior is becoming too complex for humans to understand.

AI.brief_summary: 设计一个不含正确答案的简单任务，考察混合七个模型家族的多智能体系统中哪个模型对最终共识影响最大；发现参数更大的模型会吸收其他模型的意见，并以单纯形上的加权粒子与能量景观加以解释。
AI.relevance_reason: 把共识形成刻画为加权粒子/信念状态的聚合与更新，可能为 LVR 中多 latent 假设的权重分配和证据吸收提供类比线索，但与视觉推理无直接联系，需核查其机制是否可迁移。
